In an isosceles right triangle, the altitude to the hypotenuse is half the hypotenuse.

Given the altitude is \(4\sqrt{2}\), the hypotenuse is

\[
2(4\sqrt{2})=8\sqrt{2}.
\]

For an isosceles right triangle with hypotenuse \(c\), the area is

\[
\frac{c^2}{4}.
\]

Thus,

\[
\text{Area}=\frac{(8\sqrt{2})^2}{4}
=\frac{128}{4}
=32.
\]

\[
\boxed{32}
\]
